plan.angle: synthesis revised after the coverage critic and two skeptics: 24 batches (seven oversized batches split in two), honest window estimate, one address contract for jobs, dock typing and offline guards
principles: Spine = FOUNDATION-FIRST (best on parity safety and feasibility), re-ordered so the editor frame comes right after the start-up shell (the owner sees the core product early and the biggest test churn is found early). HONEST SIZING: a batch over about 80 parity rows, or one with heavy test churn, is a scheduled pair of sub-batches that each end at a green gate: B5a/B5b, B8a/B8b, B9a/B9b, B10a/B10b, B12a/B12b, B13a/B13b, B14a/B14b (B3/B4, B6/B7 and B15/B16 were already pairs); B3 is planned as TWO windows with a checkpoint. 24 batches, about 26 windows (a window is 3 h of work plus 2 h rest, so about 5 days wall time). The one-batch-at-a-time rule is the owner's; whether Applications/Projects (B12a-B16, lazy-only) may run as a second track beside the editor batches is an owner call (default: sequential).

Parity rule first: UI only, every live function stays, new capabilities are PARKED. Ownership is by area file plus ID range; cite rows as '<file>: <ID>' (EDIT-/NEW- exist in editor-content.md and editor-design-templates.md; 'D-nn' is the DRAWN BUT NOT table of shell-docs, projects, mobile; 'Nn' is applications section 2; ELAE NEW-nn two digits). CATCH-ALL per area (the owning batch also takes any row added by review or later): editor-content -> B6, editor-design-templates -> B8a, editor-letter-ats-export -> B10a, shell-docs -> B5a, applications -> B13a, projects -> B15, mobile -> B17. Where an area is split across sub-batches the catch-all goes to the FIRST one; its lead may hand a catch-all row to a later sub-batch only by writing it into batches/B<n>.md and RUN-STATE, so the row still has exactly one owner. A row built in several batches (MOBI-160: hover-only hints) has one verifying owner (B8b) and the brief lists which batch builds which part. The coverage script (batches/coverage-check.mjs, which reads this plan) re-checks every row against the final parity files after any move.

The parity file's Fix column is the build spec and the live app wins where board and app differ. tools/brief.mjs (written in B1) turns each batch's rows (ID, live behaviour, status, fix) into docs/tracking/ui-redesign/batches/B<n>.md; every CHANGED row is flagged DO NOT BUILD AS DRAWN and the brief opens with a 'layout deltas' table (CHANGED and MISSING rows: how the drawn layout bends to hold the live function, conservative option = live control kept one menu or drawer away; EDIT-089 is listed there as 'live rule kept, owner call'). A Fix that begins 'Draw ...' (137 rows) is a canvas instruction and is printed as 'Build from the live behaviour; no board, or the board differs: design from tokens', always with the live-behaviour cell beside it; a Fix that is only 'Same.', 'Keep.' or 'Draw.' (22 rows, e.g. PROJ-164/166 sprint dialogs) is specified by the live-behaviour cell. The brief also computes each batch's 'tests that go red' by grepping the touched files and visible labels across tests/ and cypress/ and fails when a hit is not in the batch's update list. The render check compares the build with the board AND the deltas table.

Phone is built with its surface (each batch owns the desktop and phone rows of its screens). STANDING PHONE GUARD in every batch gate from B3 on: cypress/e2e/26-mobile-layout.cy.js plus tests/playwright/phone-reach.spec.mjs run in the single targeted dispatch. phone-reach runs with hasTouch and isMobile (hover: none) and reaches every control by tap only, never hover(), because the default Desktop Chrome project keeps hover and would hide hover-only controls; one case is proven by a mutation commit. Breakpoints 768 px (useIsMobile) and Tailwind sm/md/lg; the 768-1100 px band has no board and gets one rule (the editor dock overlays the stage below 1100 px, and the sidebar width is clamped while a dock is open) proven in a real browser in B4 and re-run in B17.

Start-up path has about 0 kB spare (71-startup-chunks, cap 1,100 kB of minified JS; CSS and index.html are free). BEFORE any B1 code the lead dispatches tests=71-startup-chunks and perf: startup once (raw and gzip margins; tests/perf/budgets.mjs also holds startup.gzip 450 kB and startup.largest 500 kB) and the owner is asked NOW to confirm the fallback order (default: lazy parts, then lazy jsonResumeImport, then lazy Dashboard parts, cap raise last). B1 creates headroom FIRST (lazy NewLetterModal+Dialog closure, lazy CareerHistoryPanel; reserve offset: lazy jsonResumeImport with 122 updated). Only B2, B5a and B5b add start-up JS and each keeps a bytes ledger (71 read before and after, in the report; the prefetch, error-boundary and fallback code of the lazy pieces is counted). HARD THRESHOLDS: B1 target >= +15 kB, minimum +10 kB after the reserve offset; if the total spare is still under 10 kB the lead STOPS and asks the owner before B2; B2 must end with >= 7 kB spare; B5a >= 5 kB; B5b >= 3 kB (apply reserve offsets in order, then stop and ask). Every other batch is lazy-only. Rules: never import the ui barrel from start-up code; AppBar, BottomTabBar and AuthBar import only react-router Link and named lucide icons; no new util imported by both Dashboard and a lazy chunk (it is hoisted); repeated class strings become index.css component classes. LAZY PIECES INSIDE A PAGE (NewLetterModal, CareerHistoryPanel, ImportDialog, CardMenu, jsonResumeImport) must never take a core function away offline: each has an idle-time prefetch (setTimeout fallback where requestIdleCallback is missing) plus hover/focus prefetch, sits in its own ErrorBoundary, and has an in-entry fallback (Import keeps the file input and the native picker in the entry; ResumeCard keeps plain Edit/Copy/Delete buttons when CardMenu fails; New cover letter falls back to a letter from the first source when the picker fails; Career History shows the existing notice with Try again). They do NOT use the lazyPage reload guard (it reloads the tab and would drop a rename draft); that guard stays for route pages. Each fallback has a failfirst test that rejects the import().

Single-owner files, one batch at a time (sub-batches of one area are sequential too): Editor.jsx, EditorHeader.jsx, useEditorTab.js, EditorTabContent.jsx = B3 then B4 (B4 only EditorAlerts block, phone preview states); EditorPreviewPane.jsx and usePanelResize.js = B3 (SaveStatus extraction only) then B4; DesignPanel*.jsx (not DesignPanelPhone), DesignDock.jsx body and the parity registries = B8a; TemplateGallery.jsx, TemplateThumb.jsx, DesignPanelPhone.jsx = B8b; PersonalInfoEditor*.jsx, SectionEditorCustomizer.jsx, HeaderIconPickerModal, HeaderSpacingControls = B7 (B7 also owns the Section style wiring line in SectionEditor.jsx as a named hand-over from B6); SectionEditor*.jsx, RichTextEditor.jsx, EditorResumeTab.jsx = B6; CoverLetterPanel* = B9a, generator and optimizer = B9b; AtsCheckerPanel = B10a, ExportDropdown, ShareLinkModal = B10b; AuthBar.jsx, AppBar.jsx, BottomTabBar.jsx = B2; Dashboard.jsx, ResumeCard.jsx = B1 (testid, lazy boundaries), B2 (header), B5a (body); NewResume.jsx = B5b; AppRoutes.jsx = B13a only (job address redirects, first commit, with a bytes ledger) and B11 only if a route changes; shell/TopBar, WorkspaceLayout, Sidebar = B11; JobTracker.jsx = B12a, B12b, then B13a (outlet wiring only); src/index.css = B1 additive tokens and the legacy value re-point, then in each later batch exactly ONE named cluster appends component classes. Inside a batch no two clusters own the same file (a hand-over between clusters of one batch is sequential and written in the brief). Verify every cluster file path against the tree before dispatch (correct homes: src/components/board/ProjectTabs.jsx, board/CreateIssueDialog.jsx, board/useIssueActions.jsx).

Token policy: B1 adds additive cv-* tokens and cv-* component classes (ground, surface, sunken, stage, hairline, field, ink, body, muted, faint, brand family, good/warn/bad, radii, --shadow-pop, --font-cv with Instrument Sans first, then system-ui and the emoji fallbacks). --font-sans is Tailwind's own token (Kbd uses it, and the spacing preset labels contain emoji) and is NOT redefined until the owner approves the web font in B17. In a second B1 commit (CSS only, 0 bytes) the VALUES of the legacy kit tokens are re-pointed to the cv values with class names unchanged: a grep of tests/ and cypress/ found no test pinning those hex values, the kit class-pin tests (about 74) run in the related dispatch, and every render check from B3 on then compares against the right palette. Kit Button/Tabs defaults, heights and radii never change; canvas shapes arrive as variants (B11). New screens (editor, Documents, shell pages) use cv-* classes. No web-font link in index.html: a Google Fonts request on every page load contradicts the live Privacy text and offline behaviour, so it is an owner call applied in B17 only if approved (with the Privacy text updated in the same commit).

Tests: no test runs here; CI only. Per batch: failfirst for every src commit's new tests (dispatched right after the commit lands and before another commit touches the same files, because the failfirst job reverts one commit and falls back to the parent's files when the reverse diff does not apply; the lead reads the failing test NAMES in the failfirst log, not just the fail count, so a test that fails only because the reverted tree no longer imports is not accepted; a small ci.yml step that prints the first 'not ok' lines is an owner approval, default: read the log with get_job_logs). failfirst runs only node --test, so every Playwright or Cypress guard is proven two ways: a node-level mirror (source or fake-DOM assertion of the same rule, e.g. EditorDock carries the below-1100 overlay classes and no fixed inset-0; every phone-reach testid is rendered by its component) that failfirst can prove, and a MUTATION pair on the branch (a throwaway commit that breaks the rule, a red run of the named spec, then its revert and a green run; both run ids go in the batch report). Then ONE combined targeted dispatch (new tests + every test that mounts a touched component + named playwright/cypress specs + 26-mobile-layout + phone-reach + 21-a11y.cy.js whenever its controls moved (B2, B3, B6, B7, B12a, B13a, B13b) + 71-startup-chunks when a non-lazy file was touched), then ONE full gate on the final head. New tests assert reachability and behaviour (opener found by role+name, control inside a data-testid region, same write as before, union of controls of regrouped panels equals a hard-coded walk-count, a negative twin for the old path or the parked item), never Tailwind classes; the 56 dph/dvis class-pin files are restated as the defect they guard, with evidence, never weakened. A commit carries its src change and its test (a tests-only commit cannot be failfirst'ed). Testid spine and per-runner helpers (openDesign, openAts, switchTo, openExportMenu) land in B1 so B3 changes helper bodies, not 40 specs. Known flakes: J-30 (tests/pdf/81-job-tracker-session, shard 2/6; may hit ANY batch's gate: rerun the failed shard once, record both attempts, never skip; B12a root-causes it with a deterministic reproduction), tests/pdf/102-r4-dout-09 on shard 2/6, nine files reaching the live font CDN, 164-huge-paste-linear.

Protocol refinements (no step dropped): step 1 adds (a) brief generation, (b) for B1/B2/B5a/B5b a start-up read (dispatch tests: 71-startup-chunks alone, read the '# start-up path' line), and (c) MASTER SYNC: git fetch origin master and merge origin/master into the branch (merge, not rebase, the branch is pushed), re-run the coverage script against the merged parity files, add any new or changed master row to the owning batch's catch-all through batches/B<n>.md, and re-apply a master fix to a file a closed batch already rebuilt on the branch with its own test; master is never pushed to. Step 3 render check compares against the board and the deltas table, and against tokens where no board exists (about 40 percent of surfaces are undrawn). Step 4 reviewers check every CHANGED row with a negative twin. Step 5 adds a label sweep (tools/label-inventory.mjs lists title/aria-label/placeholder/button text of touched files at base vs head; any difference must map to a parity row or be reverted; this catches the tooltip-level rows two reviewers still call unlisted). Step 7 also updates docs/knowledge/*.md paths (knowledge-docs.unit), writes a row ledger (parity ID -> test name) and an a11y-notes list (noted, never fixed). Perf: one perf: browser baseline at the start of B3 (before the editor typing path changes), a comparison at the end of B4 and in B17.

Memo and render-count discipline (PERF-4): no router hook or Link inside a memoised editor part. The save chip is a self-contained memo leaf with a DECIDED data path: EditorSaveStatus takes three primitive props (persistError, saving, savedAt) straight from Editor as a sibling element and never through EditorHeader props; it renders only on those transitions (test 173 counts it as its own labelled part with a budget of at most 2 renders per keystroke burst, 0 for the header, doc switch, ATS chip, Export menu and account bar; a negative twin: passing saving through EditorHeader must fail 173). The dock (Design or ATS) is mounted beside the Resume sidebar, unlike today's tabs, so it reads the resume through a deferred value and its panels are memoised: a keystroke in a section renders DesignPanel and AtsCheckerPanel 0 times in that commit and at most once after the pause (test 180 dock-typing). Tests 165 and 173 stay green in B3-B10b (173 is rewritten in B3 to the same intent and proven with a sabotage commit pair: an unstable prop and a Link added must fail it). Walker rule: never rename a control so two controls collapse in the parity-walker signature; keep 'Reset' in a reset control's name; keep the emoji in spacing preset labels; groups/view/rail props default to everything.

Label and behaviour contracts: keep the live 'Export' strings (47 Cypress uses; no rename to Download unless the owner approves, then one constant in tests/pdf/ui-selectors.mjs and cypress/support/selectors.js); the Export trigger stays menu-only and the import item keeps its live 'new resume' meaning; nav labels follow the canvas (Documents, Applications, Projects) through shared label constants in tests only; the sidebar, its [ shortcut and cpwtcv_sidebar_collapsed are kept (restyled) until the owner explicitly says drop; the Keyboard shortcuts dialog stays reachable by pointer for signed-out, no-cloud and touch users through an auth-independent help control in the workspace bar (B11), the avatar menu entry is an additional entry shown only on pages where ? works (workspace). The address of a job: the old /jobs/:id, /jobs/new and /jobs/:id/edit keep working as redirects to /jobs?job=ID, /jobs?job=new and /jobs?job=ID&edit=1 (B13a), so the board never remounts (RouteFrame, WorkspaceLayout and useScrollMemory key on pathname and stay untouched); ?view=summary|kanban|list keeps selecting the view.

Windows: a work window is 3 h then a 2 h rest, one batch at a time; each batch is sized for one window except B3 (two windows by design, one gate at the end). A batch that does not reach its gate spans the next window and nothing else starts. Named split points remain for B6, B11 and B14b if a window runs out. Nothing is pushed to master; each batch head is functionally complete but visually mixed, so deploy is the owner's call (after B17 by default, or after any batch's full gate if the owner wants earlier deploys and less drift from master).

Accessibility is deferred: noted in the batch reports, never planned or fixed. 44 px sizes are built only where a canvas dimension or a MOBI row says so (and listed in a11y-notes); no new Escape, focus or keyboard behaviour is built where the live control has none (the avatar menu and the dock get none; a hand-rolled hook closes on outside click and takes Escape only where the live control already has it). Commits are authored sairamgudiputi <sairamgudiputi8@gmail.com>, no trailers, no mention of Claude or AI; work goes to claude/wonderful-maxwell-vu8xqw only. Test files are numbered from 178 (177 is the highest existing): B1 178, B2 179, B3 180, B4 181, B5a 182, B5b 183, B6 184, B7 185, B8a 186, B8b 187, B9a 188, B9b 189, B10a 190, B10b 191, B11 192, B12a 193, B12b 194, B13a 195, B13b 196, B14a 197, B14b 198, B15 199, B16 200, B17 201.
